reason: Exact construction and approved extraction match, but refusal specificity, initial inventory witnesses, sink coverage and failure cleanup do not yet satisfy the strict R2 proof contract. No case was executed.

ISO1.assessment: Source construction satisfies narrow capacity gate design; runtime counter interception remains unproved.
ISO1.evidence: Real createGuidedServer receives otherwise real harness options with only capacity changed to 2. Diagnostic environment flags are checked before the attempt. Proxy delegates actual HTTPS constructor and requires a positive controller constructor count, then measures zero constructor delta. It asserts no SDK launch, claim, callback, login receipt or F source request. Capacity validation precedes ownership/TLS construction in production source. The counter does not claim absence of all possible TLS activity or physical/native memory effects.

ISO2.assessment: Real native entry, pre-original-close gate and capacity sequence are authored; actual closure and writer quiescence are unexecuted.
ISO2.evidence: A uses original SDK and native fill dispatch, with CDP method-name scalar count, password focus count and a nonempty live A PID witness. B assignment is refused CAPACITY before B claim/launch/profile. After synchronous A stop, the deliberate gate precedes browser.close(), while accepting=false, active=true and A PID live. B is refused again. Release invokes original close on browser receiver; stop waits for close completion, tracked PIDs gone and scratch absent before B assign/context. maxLive=1 is asserted. PID list is sampled at SDK launch settlement, not continuous discovery of every later descendant.

ISO3.assessment: Approved same-A actual producer/consumer sequence is authored; proof-strength and privacy gaps require repair below.
ISO3.evidence: Frozen F+S inputs/scope precede assignment. S/login PASS=A and actual submit require accepted private receipt and cookie presence. F regionVisible Operations OUTPUT is read through prepare/dispatch with SUCCEEDED and real availability. Value-free Producer uses actual admission/coordinate/origin/recipe/availability and real materialization update. F sameOrigin consumer fill and submit require one matching original public-reference receipt. Same A then reaches S/reports. Pre-stop values/secrets/prepared/edges are asserted nonempty; synchronous clearing, asynchronous closeResources clearing and disposed inventory/snapshot refusal are asserted. Only S expected password rotates; server sessions are not reset/expired. Fresh CSI-B has distinct context/scope/profile, zero S cookies and no runtime binding; real A Producer metadata is submitted under B before B credentials/read. B starts with S/reports navigation, requires S/login redirect, then same PASS identifier with B value and distinct accepted receipt. Final B inventory has no A, contains B and a distinct tag. No A echo route is called.

findings.subject: Foreign producer and context negatives accept unrelated refusal paths
findings.evidence: Both assertions require only HTTP 409. resultStatus uses closedCode solely as assertion text and never asserts it. An INPUT_IDENTITY, SCHEMA, BUSY, POLICY_DENIED or expired-context refusal could satisfy the test without reaching the original producer equality join. src/guided/runtime.ts:123 emits CONTEXT_LOST for a producer absent from B local values; the whole A context posted to B URL is refused earlier by transport session envelope identity.
findings.repair: Retain each reply and assert its exact closed refusal code: CONTEXT_LOST for genuine foreign Producer under valid unchanged B envelope, IDENTITY_MISMATCH for A context at B route. Record status/code as scalar evidence, and verify B remains live and without binding immediately afterward. Keep stale grant proof separate.

findings.subject: Inventory disposal and freshness lack required preconditions
findings.evidence: Events capture inventory size/bytes/containsA/containsB, but ISO3 never requires any pre-dispose A inventory event to contain A or be nonempty. Runtime secrets.size=1 does not prove masking inventory contained A. B inventory checks run only after B login and do not require a witness before credential delivery; containsB=true is not constrained to after actual withholding. Initial B runtime hasBinding=false is asserted, but containsA=false and initial distinct inventory tag are not explicitly asserted at that boundary.
findings.repair: Before A stop require its actual inventory tag with size/bytes greater than zero and containsA=true. Immediately after B context, before either foreign metadata or credential action, require a fresh inventory event/tag distinct from A, containsA=false and containsB=false, plus runtime containsA=false/hasBinding=false. After actual B native fill require containsB=true and containsA=false on that same B tag. Do not require initial B inventory size zero. Use only scalars and direct Map.has comparisons.

findings.subject: Both-canary scans omit actual output sinks and fail before closing on error
findings.evidence: scans covers serialized callback messages and files under journal/scratch roots with literal/UTF16LE/URI/base64 variants. There is no stdout/stderr witness; production runtime defaults diagnosticStderr to process.stderr.write. No final evidence file/output scan is performed. Failure paths enter close without scans and remove scratch/journal data. Both planted values are URI-safe, so encodeURIComponent equals the literal and supplies no distinct percent-encoded witness. No retained raw inventory snapshots, mock call archives or secret-derived hashes were found.
findings.repair: Add test-local forwarding output/diagnostic witnesses that emit scalar hit counts for both canaries and encodings without retaining chunks, preserve original receivers/arguments/returns/errors, and restore them in finally. Cover final scalar evidence serialization before writing. Scan extant roots in failure-safe cleanup before deletion, preserving the original failure. Bind encoding coverage honestly; add relevant distinct encoded variants without changing approved fixture bytes or production APIs.

findings.subject: Setup failures bypass cleanup; teardown is sequential and not bounded
findings.evidence: Each case awaits harness before entering try/finally. Failure while starting S, creating directory, patching methods or listening callbacks can leave previously acquired F/S resources and global descriptors live. SDK setup can reject after an actual context exists; options.launch then throws before returning the browser port, without local close/restore cleanup. close awaits worker.close without a bound, and later sequential cleanup skips F/S/client/sdk cleanup if an earlier callback/F close rejects. Five-second PID polling is reached only after stop HTTP response; Vitest timeout does not guarantee resource cleanup. worker remains a strong variable reference after successful close.
findings.repair: Register cleanup immediately after each acquisition inside harness and unwind on construction failure. On post-launch setup failure, attempt original browser close and descriptor restoration before rethrowing the original error. Release gate promptly; bound cleanup attempts using existing budgets, attempt all resource releases even if one fails, and surface unresolved closure rather than claiming quiescence. Restore descriptors and drop worker/browser/CDP/setup strong references in finally. Preserve real close receiver/arguments and ordinary original promise delegation; keep only the explicitly approved close gate exception.

scopeLimits: All three native cases are source constructions only; no runtime observation or passing test is asserted.
Imports bind production TypeScript source, not compiled dist runner behavior. Matching 274 stored dist hashes proves manifest stability at read time, not current source compilation equivalence.
SDK launch/private instrumentation behavior, TLS ESM interception, timer races, native counters, focus callbacks and actual process/writer closure remain unverified.
No backend/Core/Postgres/Vault CSI authorization, whole acceptance criteria, full19, ten-story QA or lifecycle closure approval. Direct stale A grant remains a separate fourth proof.
Coordinator remains sole shared build/runtime owner. No execution release follows this review.
